canonical.title: A routed one-week Greece plan from an Athens arrival, summer 2026

siblings.title: Athens non-negotiables: the summer 2026 field manual
siblings.summary: Book the 08:00 Acropolis slot, pair it with the Acropolis Museum and the Ancient Agora, and treat almost everything else in Athens as optional.

siblings.title: After Athens: Greek island clusters compared for a 3-5 day August 2026 tail
siblings.summary: One Cyclades island (Naxos or Milos) beats any two-island hop; the Saronic is the only cluster where two islands in four days is not a trap.

siblings.title: Day trips from Athens without changing base — summer 2026
siblings.summary: One spare day in August: the early hydrofoil to Hydra, or Delphi if you want antiquity — and skip Meteora and the three-island cruise entirely.

siblings.title: The mainland tail: a Peloponnese loop and/or Meteora after Athens
siblings.summary: A car-based Peloponnese loop plus Meteora is cheaper and emptier than the Cyclades in August but far hotter and more driving.

siblings.title: Athens to the islands, summer 2026: ferries, ports and when to fly instead
siblings.summary: Piraeus, Rafina or Lavrio, conventional ferry or catamaran, and the small set of legs where a domestic flight actually beats the boat.

siblings.title: Eating and Drinking in Athens and the Islands, Summer 2026
siblings.summary: Route Athens around souvlaki row, one mezedopoleio dinner and one rooftop; skip the starred night unless you want it.

sources.title: Odysseus — Acropolis of Athens (Ministry of Culture)
sources.claim: Acropolis €30 full / €15 reduced, summer hours 08:00-20:00 last entry 19:30, timed entry mandatory, 15 August a normal open day, lift out of order.

sources.title: Odysseus — Ancient Agora of Athens
sources.claim: Ancient Agora €20/€10, site plus museum, summer 08:00-19:30.

sources.title: Santorini Dave — Naxos
sources.claim: Naxos: largest and most fertile Cyclade; Portara, Venetian Kastro, Plaka and Agios Prokopios sand, Mount Zas, marble villages; often uncrowded even in summer.

sources.title: Rick Steves forum — Peloponnese road trip, 4-5 days
sources.claim: With 4 nights you cannot see everything; Areopoli is not realistically a day trip from an Argolid base.

sources.title: Dave's Travel Pages — Meltemi winds
sources.claim: Meltemi blows June-September, peaks July-August at 7-8 Beaufort, strengthens mid-morning, eases by sunset, runs in spells of up to a week; Mykonos, Tinos and Andros worst hit.

sources.title: Wego — Greece heatwave
sources.claim: July 2026 heatwave: central Greece 43.5 °C, eastern Peloponnese 41-42 °C, Aegean islands 28-30 °C.

sources.title: Teleporio — Meltemi wind ferry guide
sources.claim: High-speed catamarans cancel before large Blue Star hulls; take 07:00-08:00 departures over 14:00-16:00; build buffer days.

sources.title: Art Visit Guide — Archaeological sites in Athens
sources.claim: The seven ex-combo sites now cost roughly €105 bought individually; Ancient Agora is the best value after the Acropolis; Temple of Olympian Zeus visible from the fence.

sources.title: Ephorate of Antiquities of Athens — Kerameikos notice
sources.claim: Kerameikos closed since 5 May 2025 for works, 'till further announcement'.

sources.title: Greek Reporter — Odeon of Herodes Atticus restoration
sources.claim: Odeon of Herodes Atticus closed from July 2026 for a multi-year restoration.

sources.title: Acropolis Restoration Service (YSMA)
sources.claim: Parthenon west façade scaffolding struck permanently on 15 June 2026, first time in ~220 years.

sources.title: GTP — August Full Moon 2026
sources.claim: Friday 28 August 2026: 126 sites and museums free from ~19:30 to ~23:00, extra events 26-27 and 29-30 August.

sources.title: Santorini Dave — Cyclades islands
sources.claim: Cyclades guidance is at least three nights per island.

sources.title: Greeka — Hydra ferries
sources.claim: Piraeus-Hydra 1h05-2h with 6-8 daily high-speed runs; Hydra-Poros 25-40 min €21.50; Hydra-Spetses 30-60 min €18; no direct Hydra-Aegina sailing.

sources.title: Athens Travel Guides — Athens to Hydra
sources.claim: 07:30/08:00 hydrofoil, return 17:00/18:30 gives 7-8 hours ashore; €60-120 all-in; water taxis €8-15; cars banned.

sources.title: Go-Ferry — Greek ferries booking trends
sources.claim: Book 2-3 months ahead for July/August, 3-4 months for cabins or vehicles.

sources.title: Cycladic Spaces — 15 August in Greece
sources.claim: Dekapentavgoustos is Greece's biggest domestic travel day: ports pack out, ferries sell out, timetables shift, Tinos absorbs thousands of pilgrims.

sources.title: Greek Trip Planner — trip costs
sources.claim: Mid-tier islands €80-150/room in Jul-Aug against €150-280 on Santorini or Mykonos; 50-100% accommodation premium; inter-Cyclades hops €10-20.

sources.title: Ferryhopper — Piraeus routes and fares
sources.claim: Piraeus fares and durations 2026: Aegina 30 min-1h30 €9.50, Hydra 1-2 h €15, Milos €33, Paros €40.50, Naxos 3h15-6h €42, Mykonos €43, Santorini 3h55-8h €39, Heraklion 7-13 h €27.50, Rhodes 12-22 h €46.50.

sources.title: Santorini Dave — Athens transportation
sources.claim: Metro Line 3 to Piraeus 50-60 min ~€9 beats the X96 bus at 90-120 min; allow 2 hours door-to-quay.

sources.title: Athens Tourism — Athens to the islands ferry guide
sources.claim: Piraeus has 12 gates E1-E12 and your gate is printed on the ticket; leave 60-90 minutes at the gate; book Cyclades ferries 2-4 weeks ahead, 2-3 months for cabins.

sources.title: Blue Star Ferries — Piraeus port map
sources.claim: E1 for Santorini/Crete/Dodecanese, E6 and E7 for Cyclades departures, E9 for Saronic high-speeds to Aegina, Hydra and Spetses.

sources.title: FerryGoGo — Piraeus, Rafina or Lavrio
sources.claim: Piraeus serves Cyclades, Crete, Dodecanese, Saronic and NE Aegean; off an international flight allow at least 4 h to a Rafina sailing and 5 h to Piraeus.

sources.title: MyArtemida — airport bus to Rafina
sources.claim: KTEL airport-Rafina about 30 minutes, €4-5.50 cash, roughly hourly, first 04:30 and last 23:00.

sources.title: Greece Trips — when a ferry is cancelled
sources.claim: EU Regulation 1177/2010 gives reimbursement within seven days or re-routing at no extra cost; weather is an extraordinary circumstance so the operator owes the fare, not your hotel or missed flight.

sources.title: Santorini Dave — Greek ferries
sources.claim: Blue Star deck seats rarely sell out; SeaJets seats, cabins and vehicle spaces routinely do in July-August; operators notify cancellations by email/SMS.

sources.title: Euronews — Acropolis visitor cap and staggered entry
sources.claim: 20,000 visitors a day split into hourly quotas: 3,000 in the 08:00-09:00 hour, 2,000 in 09:00-10:00; about half of traffic arrives 08:00-noon.

sources.title: Wego — Athens heatwave
sources.claim: During the 18-22 July 2026 heatwave (40-43 °C) the Culture Ministry closed the Acropolis roughly midday to 17:00; August 2026 expected to run hotter than July; alerts via EMY and 112.

sources.title: Earth Trekkers — How to visit the Acropolis
sources.claim: Timed tickets book the gate, not the security screening, which runs 15-30 minutes at peak; be at the gate for 07:45.

sources.title: National Archaeological Museum — visit
sources.claim: Wed-Mon 08:00-20:00, Tue 13:00-20:00 (4 May-15 Nov); EU citizens under 25 free with ID.

sources.title: Tornos News — National Archaeological Museum fee
sources.claim: National Archaeological Museum entry rose to €20 on 1 January 2026, up from €12.

sources.title: Third Eye Traveller — Filopappou Hill
sources.claim: Filopappou is free and open 24/7, 15-20 minutes' walk from the Acropolis, the head-on Parthenon shot at sunset; Areopagus is polished to glass and mobbed at sunset.

sources.title: Grand PL — Mount Lycabettus
sources.claim: Lycabettus funicular €10 return / €7 one-way, every 30 minutes 09:00-02:30, from Kolonaki; free on foot in about 45 minutes.

sources.title: This is Athens — Plaka guide
sources.claim: Plaka is commercialised and crowded midday — the city's own guide says be prepared for the crowds; Anafiotika is a Cycladic micro-village built by workmen from Anafi.

sources.title: Athens Travel Guides — best souvlaki
sources.claim: Kostas in Plaka: pork souvlaki €3.50, cash only, closes 3-4pm when the meat runs out; O Thanasis kebab since 1964; Elvis in Psyrri going at 3am.

sources.title: Athens Tourism — Varvakios Agora
sources.claim: Varvakios Agora on Athinas St, since 1886, 100+ butcher stalls and 150 fish stalls, Mon-Sat 07:00-18:00, with cook-house tavernas inside.

sources.title: World's 50 Best — where to eat, drink and stay in Athens
sources.claim: O Lolos in Koukaki for fried squid and next-level dips; Kostas and Lefteris o Politis for pita; Baba au Rum on the World's 50 Best Bars list.

sources.title: Athens Glance — rooftop bars
sources.claim: A for Athens €12-15 and 360 Cocktail Bar €10-13 for the Acropolis view; GB Roof Garden €22+ cocktails; railing tables are first-come, be up by 6pm.

sources.title: The Greece Guides — Milos beaches
sources.claim: Kleftiko is boat-only, €35-50 full-day tours from Adamas; most south-coast beaches need a car or ATV.

sources.title: Discover Cyclades — Sifnos guide
sources.claim: Sifnos has 100+ km of marked trails over 19 routes and the classic 4-hour Apollonia-Kastro-Platis Gialos walk.

sources.title: Greek Trip Planner — Sifnos restaurants
sources.claim: Sifnos is the food island: clay-pot revithada, birthplace of Nikolaos Tselementes, highest chef-per-capita density in Greece.

sources.title: It's All Trip To Me — Peloponnese road trip
sources.claim: Athens airport to Ancient Corinth ~1h30 on the A8; Corinth to Nafplio ~1 h; Nafplio to Mycenae and to Epidaurus 30 min each; Monemvasia to Pounta ~1 h.

sources.title: Vriskoapostasi — Nafplio route distances
sources.claim: Nafplio to Mystras 127 km / 2h07; Mystras to Monemvasia 93 km / 1h53; Nafplio to Monemvasia direct 231 km / 3h29 with €8.55 tolls.

sources.title: Time Travel Turtle — Mystras
sources.claim: Mystras €20, open 08:00-20:00 to 31 August, wants about two hours, and is a hard uphill walk from the lower gate — start at the top.

sources.title: Visit Greece — Epidaurus Festival 2026
sources.claim: The Epidaurus Festival runs 20 June - 29 August 2026 in the ancient theatre, with Antigone 7-8 Aug, Lysistrata 21-22 Aug and Ion 28-29 Aug.

sources.title: Best Greece Tours — site hours and fees
sources.claim: Mycenae, Epidaurus, Olympia and Delphi €12 each; Ancient Corinth €8; summer opening broadly 08:00-19:30.

sources.title: Greeka blog — road trip to the Mani
sources.claim: Mani back roads average about 60 km/h; Areopoli to Kalamata under 2 h; Athens to Kardamyli 273 km / 3h17.

sources.title: Martins — Voidokilia beach guide
sources.claim: Voidokilia is free and unorganised — no sunbeds, umbrellas or canteen, a dirt-road park-up plus a 5-minute dune walk, and jammed 11:00-18:00 in August.

sources.title: TollGuru — Greece motorway tolls
sources.claim: Athens-Corinth tolls €13.80-19.50 and Corinth-Kalamata about €11.75 at January 2026 rates; an e-pass saves 8-15%.

sources.title: Greece Moments — car rental
sources.claim: Car rental €50-100/day in August plus €5-12/day zero-excess cover, petrol about €2.00-2.10/L.

sources.title: Dave's Travel Pages — Athens to Meteora
sources.claim: The direct Athens-Kalambaka train is suspended until late 2026/mid-2027; what remains is a 4h30 express coach at €54 each way. 'I personally wouldn't do it… it's a LONG day!'

sources.title: Athens Travel Guides — Saronic islands cruise
sources.claim: The one-day three-island cruise is ~11 hours (07:00-18:00) at €110-130 for 1 h at Poros, 1.5 h at Hydra and 2 h at Aegina.

sources.title: Delphi Tours — Athens to Delphi
sources.claim: Organised Delphi coaches are 2.5 h each way, 8-10 h total, €33-84 with entry included.

sources.title: Real Greek Experiences — Temple of Poseidon at Sounion
sources.claim: KTEL from opposite Pedion tou Areos, about 2 h, €6.30 each way; site open 09:30 to sunset, €20 summer entry.

sources.title: Athens Travel Guides — Cape Sounion day trip
sources.claim: 'Almost zero shade at the site. Zero.' Go for the ~20:15-20:45 summer sunset; tours cost €50-70.

sources.title: Greeka — Aegina ferries
sources.claim: Aegina is 40 minutes and €11.50-19.50 each way with 9+ daily high-speed departures.

sources.title: Greeka — Hydra
sources.claim: Hydra bans cars outright — movement is on foot, by donkey or by water taxi; the draw is stone mansions and a pedestrian harbour.

sources.title: Greek Trip Planner — overtourism data
sources.claim: Santorini runs about 220:1 visitors-to-residents and Mykonos 180-200:1, against 3:1-15:1 on Naxos, Sifnos, Milos and Folegandros; Crete is diluted at 8-10:1.

sources.title: Real Greek Experiences — island hopping in the Cyclades
sources.claim: The Cyclades run on two effectively separate ferry lines; build buffer days and avoid rigid one-night-per-island schedules in peak season; prefer large vehicle ferries.

sources.title: Archaeology Travel — buying Acropolis tickets
sources.claim: The €30 five-day combined ticket is abolished; a timed ticket is valid from 15 minutes before to 15 minutes after its slot.

sources.title: Athens Travel Guides — Acropolis Museum guide
sources.claim: The Parthenon Gallery is rotated 23° to align with the real thing; Friday's 22:00 close puts it in sunset light with the floodlit temple through the glass.

sources.title: Blue Star Ferries — web check-in
sources.claim: Web check-in opens 48 h and closes 2 h before departure, issuing a QR e-ticket shown with ID or passport.

sources.title: Ferryhopper — Athens to Hydra
sources.claim: Up to 12 daily sailings on the Athens-Hydra route.

sources.title: hhticket.gr — Hellenic Heritage official ticketing
sources.claim: The Ministry of Culture's own booking platform, with no booking fee.

sources.title: TNT Magazine — Greek visitor caps 2026
sources.claim: Santorini's cruise cap is 8,000 passengers/day and a €20 levy applies at Santorini and Mykonos 1 June-30 September, but ferry and flight arrivals are not capped.

sources.title: Athens Epidaurus Festival — Odeon farewell
sources.claim: June 2026 was the Odeon's farewell season before restoration works starting July 2026.

sources.title: Ferryhopper — Greek islands ferry schedules 2026
sources.claim: The Ionian is not ferry-reachable from any Athens port; the Sporades are reached via Volos, Mantoudi or Kymi.

sources.title: Take Me To Greece — Kaisariani Monastery
sources.claim: Kaisariani €3, 08:30-16:00, closed Tuesdays, bus 224 from Syntagma then a 40-minute uphill walk, shaded cypress grounds.

sources.title: Athens Tourism — tram to the coast
sources.claim: Tram T3 reaches Glyfada in 35-45 min or Voula in 50-60 min on a €1.20 90-minute integrated ticket, with free public beaches at Edem, Kalamaki and parts of Glyfada.

sources.title: Athens Tourism — Mycenae and Epidaurus day trip
sources.claim: Mycenae and Epidaurus open 08:00, €12 summer combined ticket at each, fully exposed at 35 °C+ in August; self-drive €60-100/day plus €15 tolls.

sources.title: Greek Trip Planner — islands for beaches and food
sources.claim: Naxos is produce and dairy — small creamy potatoes, aged graviera, ximomizithra, kopanisti.

sources.title: Rick Steves forum — Naxos, Paros or Milos
sources.claim: Even Naxos, Paros and Milos are among the five most-visited Cyclades — 'quieter' is relative.
